arabic: تَجَاهَلَ الْمُشْرِفُ اعْتِرَاضَ الطَّالِبِ عَلَى تَحْدِيدِ مَكَانِ الاِمْتِحَانِ، وَلَمْ يَرْضَ الطَّالِبُ.
english: The supervisor ignored the student's objection to fixing the location of the exam, and the student was not satisfied.
old_reason: Grammatical and plausible scenario; translation accurate.
reason: Correct, coherent sentence about a supervisor ignoring an objection.

arabic: لَمْ يَتَجَاهَلِ الطَّالِبُ شُحُوبَ جَارِهِ، فَحَمَلَهُ إِلَى عِيَادَةٍ لِرِعَايَتِهِ.
english: The student did not ignore his neighbor's pallor, so he carried him to a clinic for care.
old_reason: Plausible: noticing neighbor's pallor and taking him to a clinic. Translation fine.
reason: Grammatical. Carrying a pale neighbor to a clinic is understandable. 'لِرِعَايَتِهِ' is slightly stiff but fine.

arabic: تَوَقَّعْتُ لُغْزًا فِي هَذِهِ الْأُسْطُورَةِ، لَكِنَّ سُطُورَهَا لَغْوٌ بِلَا تَشْوِيقٍ.

old_reason: Forced combination; 'سطورها لغو بلا تشويق' is awkward and contrived, expecting a riddle in a legend is odd.
reason: Understandable and grammatical. لَغْوٌ means nonsense and سطور means lines, so the sentence is acceptable.

arabic: هَاتِ يَا اِبْنِي نِصْفَ الزُّبْدَةِ وَرُبْعَ وِعَاءِ الخَرْدَلِ مِنَ الخِزَانَةِ.
english: Son, bring me half the butter and a quarter of the mustard jar from the cupboard.
old_reason: Asking for 'half the butter and a quarter of the mustard jar' is odd; 'هات' with 'يا ابني' fine, but quantity of a jar is contrived and missing 'لي'. Reads as forced word-list.
reason: Correct Arabic. هات is colloquial but acceptable. Asking for half the butter and a quarter of a mustard jar is an odd request.

arabic: شِرَاءُ التَّنُّورَةِ مُتْعِبٌ، فَالمَقَاسُ خَاطِئٌ وَالحَجْمُ صَغِيرٌ جِدًّا.
english: Buying the skirt is tiring, since the size is wrong and the fit is too small.
old_reason: 'المقاس خاطئ والحجم صغير' is redundant; translation 'fit is too small' conflates size/fit. Also 'buying is tiring' is contrived.
reason: Grammatical and ordinary. 'The fit is too small' renders الحجم صغير loosely, but the meaning is close.

arabic: أَضَافَ الطَّالِبُ حَفْنَةً مِنَ السُّكَّرِ إِلَى خَلِيطِ الزُّبْدَةِ وَالزَّيْتِ.
english: The student added a handful of sugar to the butter and oil mixture.
old_reason: Simple, coherent cooking sentence; translation accurate.
reason: Correct and ordinary baking scene.

arabic: نَاوَلَتْنِي الجَارَةُ حَفْنَةً مِنَ القَمْحِ وَخَلِيطًا مِنَ الزُّبْدَةِ وَالسُّكَّرِ.
english: The neighbor handed me a handful of wheat and a mixture of butter and sugar.
old_reason: Neighbor handing a handful of wheat and a butter-sugar mixture is an odd, list-like combination.
reason: Correct Arabic, but a neighbor handing over wheat and a butter-sugar mixture is an odd scene.

arabic: الطَّحَّانُ الصَّبُورُ كَنَسَ الْمَطْحَنَةَ، ثُمَّ أَغْلَقَ الْبَوَّابَةَ فِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ.
english: The patient miller swept the mill, then closed the gate that day.
old_reason: Coherent narrative sentence; grammatical and accurate.
reason: Correct and coherent. The final phrase 'that day' is slightly filler but fine.

arabic: رَمَّ النَّجَّارُ فِي الجَرَاجِ مُؤَخَّرَةَ العَرَبَةِ وَعَجَلَتَهَا بِقَضِيبٍ خَاصٍّ.
english: In the garage, the carpenter repaired the rear of the cart and its wheel with a special rod.
old_reason: Carpenter repairing cart with 'a rod' is awkward; 'رم' and 'الجراج' plus 'قضيب خاص' are contrived and the sentence is forced.
reason: رَمَّ means to repair and is attested. The sentence is grammatical, but repairing a cart with a 'rod' in a garage is odd.

arabic: الْمَنْسَفُ أَكْلِي الْمُفَضَّلُ، لَكِنَّ الصَّيَّادِيَةَ عِنْدَ هَذَا الطَّبَّاخِ الْبَارِعِ تُضَاهِيهِ.
english: Mansaf is my favorite food, but this skillful cook’s sayadieh rivals it.
old_reason: Plausible comparison of mansaf and sayadieh (a fish dish); grammatical. Translation accurate.
reason: Correct sentence about mansaf and sayadieh. Loanword food names are fine.

arabic: نَمَّ بَعْضُ الأَصْدِقَاءِ عَلَى العَزْبَاءِ، لَكِنَّهَا دَافَعَتْ عَنِ اسْتِغْنَائِهَا عَنِ الرَّجُلِ بِعِنَادٍ.
english: Some friends gossiped about the single woman, but she stubbornly defended her not needing a man.
old_reason: Grammatical and plausible; 'نم على' means gossip/inform on, acceptable. Translation fine.
reason: نَمَّ عَلَى is attested for gossiping or informing on someone. The grammar is fine, but the content is somewhat forced.

arabic: فِي الصَّبَاحِ، أَيْقَظَتِ الأَمِيرَةُ جَوَادَهَا بِقُبْلَةٍ، وَدَاعَبَتْهُ، ثُمَّ هَمَسَتْ: أَهْلًا.
english: In the morning, the princess woke her horse with a kiss, stroked it, and then whispered: "Hello."
old_reason: Charming, plausible story sentence; grammatical and accurate.
reason: Correct Arabic with a fairy-tale scene of a princess and her horse.

arabic: عَجِبَ الْوَلَدُ بُرْهَةً مِنْ ضِيَاءِ الْهِلَالِ الَّذِي لَمْ يَأْفُلْ.
english: For a moment, the boy marveled at the glow of the crescent that had not yet set.
old_reason: Grammatical, literary but plausible. عجب من is fine; يأفل (set) used correctly for the crescent.
reason: عَجِبَ مِن، أَفَلَ for setting of the moon; correct and poetic.

arabic: تَسَلَّقَ السِّنْجَابُ العِمَارَةَ فِي بُرْهَةٍ، فَدَهِشَ الوَلَدُ وَالرَّجُلُ أَيْضًا.
english: The squirrel climbed the building in a moment, and the boy and the man were both astonished.
old_reason: A squirrel climbing a building 'in a moment' is odd but plausible; however 'بُرْهَة' means a span of time, not an instant, and 'فِي بُرْهَةٍ' is awkward. Also 'دَهِشَ الوَلَدُ وَالرَّجُلُ' is okay, but the overall phrasing is unnatural.
reason: Correct Arabic; a squirrel climbing a building in a moment is odd but understandable.

arabic: المَنْسَفُ أَكْلِي المُفَضَّلُ، وَأَنَا مُولَعٌ جِدّاً بِالبَهَارِ وَالنَّعْنَاعِ.
english: Mansaf is my favorite food, and I am very fond of spices and mint.
old_reason: Natural, grammatical. Mansaf as favorite food and fondness for spices and mint is plausible.
reason: Fine nominal sentence; مولع بـ is correct. أكلي المفضل is acceptable.

arabic: تَذَمَّرَ الطِّفْلُ الآنَ لِأَنَّ فِي حَنْجَرَتِهِ خَدَرًا وَلُعَابُهُ مَالِحٌ.
english: The child is complaining now because there is numbness in his throat and his saliva is salty.
old_reason: Forced combination of symptoms (numb throat, salty saliva) with 'now' and a child complaining; reads like a word-list sentence and is implausible phrasing.
reason: خَدَر in the throat with salty saliva as a reason for complaining is odd; 'تذمر الآن' is awkward and the clause reads as assembled from symptoms.

arabic: دَعَمَ الْوَزِيرُ إِيقَافَ حَبْسِ الْفَقِيرِ الْبَائِسِ لِأَنَّ حَالَتَهُ مُؤْلِمَةٌ.
english: The minister supported stopping the imprisonment of the miserable poor man because his case is painful.
old_reason: Grammatical and plausible news-style sentence; translation accurate.
reason: Grammatical and understandable; the minister supporting an end to imprisonment is plausible.

arabic: لَمْ يَحْصُلِ الطَّالِبُ عَلَى مُحْتَوًى إِنْجِلِيزِيٍّ مَجَّانِيٍّ فِي هَذِهِ الْقَنَاةِ.
english: The student did not get free English content on this channel.
old_reason: Grammatical, plausible statement about a channel; 'free English content' matches.
reason: Correct grammar and agreement; natural statement.

arabic: طَلَبْتُ سَنْدَوِيتْشَ طَاوُوقٍ وَمُقَبِّلَاتٍ بِالنَّعْنَاعِ، لَكِنَّ الطَّاوُوقَ كَانَ مُتَجَمِّدًا.
english: I ordered a tawook sandwich and appetizers with mint, but the tawook was frozen.
old_reason: Coherent restaurant scenario with a complaint; grammatical and accurately translated.
reason: Everyday restaurant scene with loanword sandwich; correct.

arabic: شَاهَدْنَا فِلْمًا مُضْحِكًا جِدًّا، فَتَحَوَّلَ مِزَاجُ بَابَا المُرْهَقِ إِلَى سُرُورٍ.
english: We watched a very funny film, and Dad's tired mood turned into happiness.
old_reason: Natural and coherent; 'بابا' is colloquial but fine. Translation accurate.
reason: Colloquial بابا is allowed; sentence is correct and ordinary.

arabic: رَغِبَ الجَارُ اللَّهِمُ فِي كُلِّ طَعَامِ المَأْدُبَةِ: الرُّزِّ المَنْدِي وَالفُلْفُلِ المَحْشِيِّ.
english: The greedy neighbor wanted all the food at the feast: the mandi rice and the stuffed peppers.
old_reason: 'اللَّهِم' is not a standard word for greedy (should be نَهِم); also the apposition الرُّزِّ/الفُلْفُلِ after 'طعام' is case-wrong (should be genitive and the list is forced); error-prone.
reason: اللهم is the wrong form (should be اللَّهِم, but رغب في for wanting food is off); also the apposition after كل طعام is in genitive but الرُّزِّ and الفلفل should be fine... main issue: رَغِبَ فِي is an unnatural collocation for desiring food and the list reads as word-list assembly.

arabic: النَّمِرُ قَفَزَ عَلَى الْحَارِسِ بِضَرَاوَةٍ، لَكِنَّ الْحَارِسَ نَجَا بِحِيلَةٍ.
english: The tiger leaped fiercely at the guard, but the guard escaped using a trick.
old_reason: Grammatical, coherent story-like sentence; translation accurate.
reason: Correct Arabic; a tiger attacking a guard is dramatic but understandable.

arabic: الْهَمْسْتَرُ الْمَنْفُوشُ مُتَثَاقِلٌ، لَكِنَّهُ تَحَرَّكَ مِنْ وَسَطِ الْمِخَدَّةِ إِلَى رُكْنِهَا.
english: The fluffy hamster is sluggish, but it moved from the middle of the pillow to its corner.
old_reason: A hamster moving across a pillow with 'sluggish' as a state is a forced combination; the scenario is contrived and word-list-like.
reason: Correct Arabic; hamster crossing a pillow is odd but fine.

arabic: مَقَرُّ الْمِعْمَارِ فِي هَذَا الصَّرْحِ الْإِدَارِيِّ الْبَعِيدِ عَنِ الْمَتْحَفِ.
english: The architect’s headquarters is in this administrative building far from the museum.
old_reason: Catalog-style fragment with no verb or predicate; 'المعمار' means architecture/architect ambiguously, and the sentence is incomplete as a proposition.
reason: Grammatical nominal sentence; مِعْمَار attested for architect; the situation is slightly odd.

arabic: لَدَى الرَّجُلِ عِمَارَةٌ عَلَى مَسَافَةٍ مِنَ الجِسْرِ، وَثَمَنُهَا نِصْفُ مِلْيُونِ دُولَارٍ.
english: The man has a building some distance from the bridge, and its price is half a million dollars.
old_reason: Grammatical and plausible statement about owning a building; translation accurate.
reason: عِمَارَة means building; 'عَلَى مَسَافَةٍ مِنَ الجِسْرِ' is fine. Ordinary sentence.

arabic: شَافَ الوَلَدُ فَرَاشَةً عَلَى سَبَّابَتِهِ، فَدَهِشَ وَصَمَتَ بُرْهَةً.
english: The boy saw a butterfly on his index finger, so he was astonished and fell silent for a moment.
old_reason: Coherent scene; شاف is colloquial but acceptable; translation matches.
reason: Colloquial شاف is accepted. The rest is correct. A butterfly on a finger is a charming but slightly unusual scene.

arabic: كَثْرَةُ ظُهُورِ هَذَا الْمَغْرُورِ فِي الْمُسَلْسَلِ مُمِلَّةٌ جِدًّا لِي.
english: This arrogant man's frequent appearances in the series are very boring to me.
old_reason: Plausible complaint about an arrogant character appearing too often; grammar fine (كثرة ... مملة).
reason: كثرة is feminine singular, so مملة agrees. However, 'مغرور' as a bare demonstrative noun and 'مملة لي' is awkward. Also مُمِلَّة is fine, but the phrase is stiff. Overall it is understandable and grammatical, so it should be accepted instead.

arabic: الرِّجَالُ عَبَدُوا آلِهَةً، ثُمَّ تَحَوَّلُوا بَعْدَ قَرْنٍ وَعَبَدُوا إِلٰهًا وَاحِدًا.
english: The men worshipped gods, then after a century they changed and worshipped one God.
old_reason: Grammatical, plausible historical/religious statement; translation accurate.
reason: Grammatical. عبدوا آلهة then إلهًا واحدًا is fine. Translation matches.

arabic: فِي الْجَرَاجِ، مَنَعَ الْمُهَنْدِسُ عَبَثَ الْغُلَامِ بِعَجَلَةِ الْعَرَبَةِ الْقَدِيمَةِ.
english: In the garage, the engineer stopped the boy from tampering with the old cart's wheel.
old_reason: Forced combination: an engineer stopping a boy from tampering with an old cart's wheel in a garage is contrived; الجراج with عربة قديمة feels word-list driven.
reason: Colloquial جراج is accepted. منع عبث الغلام بعجلة is correct. A boy tampering with a cart wheel is an unusual scene.

arabic: مَا زَالَ الخَدَرُ فِي حَلْقِي، مَعَ أَنَّ الإِجْرَاءَ لَمْ يَكُنْ مُعَقَّدًا.
english: My throat is still numb, even though the procedure was not complicated.
old_reason: Natural statement after a medical procedure; translation accurate.
reason: Correct: الخدر means numbness, الإجراء means procedure, and ما زال is used properly.

arabic: بَعْدَ غَسْلِ الوَجْهِ، مَسَحَ الوَلَدُ حَاجِبَهُ، لَكِنَّ اللَّزْقَةَ كَانَتْ مُلْتَصِقَةً بِهِ.
english: After washing his face, the boy wiped his eyebrow, but the plaster was still stuck to it.
old_reason: The Arabic says the plaster was stuck to it, but 'still' is added in the English; also wiping an eyebrow with a plaster stuck is awkward. Mismatch and contrived.
reason: Arabic is correct, but 'was still stuck' adds 'still'. كانت ملتصقة means 'was stuck'. This is a minor difference. Also لزقة means plaster, which is fine.

arabic: الْهَمْسْتَرُ الْمَنْفُوشُ مُولَعٌ بِالْإِجَّاصِ، وَهُوَ الْآنَ فِي هَذَا الرُّكْنِ.
english: The fluffy hamster loves pears, and he is in this corner now.
old_reason: Simple coherent sentence about a pet hamster; translation accurate.
reason: Correct grammar. مولع بـ means fond of. A hamster loving pears is a quirky scene.

arabic: وَجَدَ الرَّجُلُ تَجْعِيدَةً فَظِيعَةً فِي الجَلَّابِيَّةِ وَفِي الجِينْزِ، فَدَمْدَمَ.
english: The man found a terrible wrinkle in the robe and in the jeans, so he grumbled.
old_reason: Finding a wrinkle in both a jalabiyya and jeans at once is a forced word-list combination; unnatural.
reason: Grammatical. تجعيدة means wrinkle and دمدم means grumbled. A wrinkle in both a robe and jeans is a slightly odd scene.

arabic: لَمْ يَرْغَبِ البَطَلُ فِي الصِّرَاعِ فَسَالَمَ الشِّرِّيرَ، لَكِنَّ الشِّرِّيرَ خَادَعَهُ.
english: The hero did not desire conflict, so he made peace with the villain, but the villain deceived him.
old_reason: Coherent story-like sentence; grammar correct; translation accurate.
reason: Correct. سالم means made peace with, and خادع means deceived. Ordinary story sentence.

arabic: تَصَوَّرَ الطَّالِبُ العَجَمِيُّ أَنَّ الأَبْجَدِيَّةَ الإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةَ مُعَقَّدَةٌ جِدّاً فَتَذَمَّرَ.
english: The foreign student imagined that the English alphabet was very complex, so he complained.
old_reason: العجمي (non-Arab/Persian) rendered as 'foreign student' is odd, and a non-Arab student finding the English alphabet complex is contrived; the word choice is unnatural.
reason: Correct. العجمي means non-Arab, so 'foreign' is acceptable. Grammar and logic are fine.

arabic: يَمْنَحُ الطِّبُّ الحَدِيثُ المُوَاطِنَ رِعَايَةً وَشِفَاءً مِنَ المَرَضِ.
english: Modern medicine gives the citizen care and recovery from disease.
old_reason: Grammatical, plausible formal statement; translation accurate.
reason: Correct and clear. يمنح with two objects is fine. Textbook-style.

arabic: كَنَسَتِ الفَتَاةُ فَضْلَةَ الهَمْسْتَرِ وَالجُرَذِ بِالمِكْنَسَةِ، ثُمَّ مَسَحَتِ الأَرْضَ.
english: The girl swept up the droppings of the hamster and the rat with the broom, then wiped the floor.
old_reason: Plausible household cleaning scene; grammar fine (فضلة as droppings is acceptable, though روث/فضلات more usual).
reason: Correct Arabic; sweeping hamster and rat droppings together is an odd scene. فضلة is acceptable for droppings.

arabic: إِنَّ ذِكْرَى إِيَابِ ابْنِهَا مُؤَثِّرَةٌ جِدًّا، وَقَدْ بَاحَتْ بِهَا لِجَارَتِهَا.
english: The memory of her son’s return is very moving, and she has confided it to her neighbor.
old_reason: باحت بها: 'ذكرى' is not something one confides; باح بسرّ. Collocation is awkward and illogical (confiding a memory being moving).
reason: باح with a memory is not a valid collocation (باح is for secrets).

arabic: يَاتُرَى مَا حَجْمُ ثَرْوَةِ صَاحِبِ العِمَارَةِ، وَهَلِ امْتَلَكَهَا بِنَزَاهَةٍ؟
english: I wonder how large the wealth of the building's owner is, and did he come to own it with integrity?
old_reason: Natural rhetorical wondering; 'يا ترى' is common colloquially and grammar is fine.
reason: يا ترى is acceptable; sentence is coherent and translation accurate.

arabic: الرِّعَايَةُ هَامَّةٌ لِلشِّفَاءِ مِنْ هَذَا الْمَرَضِ، لَكِنَّ الْمُعَانَاةَ بَاقِيَةٌ.
english: Care is important for recovery from this disease, but the suffering persists.
old_reason: Coherent, grammatical, accurate.
reason: Correct, clear sentence with accurate translation.

arabic: كَانَ الطَّحَّانُ صَبُورًا مَعَ الْمَأْمُورِ الْمُؤَنِّبِ، ثُمَّ دَمْدَمَ وَغَادَرَ الْمَخْبَزَ.
english: The miller was patient with the scolding officer, then muttered and left the bakery.
old_reason: Odd scenario: a miller scolded by an officer in a bakery; the word combination feels forced from a word list.
reason: Grammatical; a miller leaving a bakery after being scolded by an officer is an odd scene.

arabic: لَمْ يَكُنْ هُنَاكَ اعْتِرَاضٌ عَلَى تَصْنِيفِ المُحْتَوَى فِي المَادَّةِ التَّاسِعَةِ.
english: There was no objection to the classification of the content in the ninth article.
old_reason: Plausible legal/regulatory statement about content classification in an article; grammatical.
reason: Correct formal/legal register sentence; translation accurate.

arabic: النَّجَّارُ مُتَخَصِّصٌ فِي صِنَاعَةِ عَجَلَاتِ الْعَرَبَاتِ مِنَ الزَّانِ فِي هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ.
english: The carpenter specializes in making cart wheels from beech wood in this city.
old_reason: Coherent sentence; الزان is beech; plausible though slightly textbook.

arabic: حِكَايَةُ المُسَلْسَلِ مُمْتِعَةٌ وَمُؤَثِّرَةٌ، فَشَاهَدَتْهَا مَجْمُوعَةُ الأَصْحَابِ كُلَّ صَبَاحٍ.
english: The series' story is enjoyable and moving, so the group of friends watched it every morning.
old_reason: Fine sentence; story of the series is enjoyable and friends watched it each morning.
reason: Fine sentence; watching every morning is a bit unusual but ordinary.

arabic: هَاتِ يَا بَابَا الشَّوْكَةَ وَالخَرْدَلَ وَالزُّبْدَةَ، فَالبَاذِنْجَانُ جَاهِزٌ الآنَ.
english: Dad, bring the fork, the mustard and the butter, the eggplant is ready now.
old_reason: Natural family dinner request; هات imperative fine, 'يا بابا' colloquial but plausible.
reason: Grammatical with colloquial بابا accepted; the list of fork, mustard, butter with eggplant is odd.

arabic: فِي مُؤَخَّرَةِ الْجَرَاجِ، رَمَّ الْمُهَنْدِسُ الْعَرَبَةَ وَأَنْزَلَ مِنْهَا قَضِيبًا.
english: At the back of the garage, the engineer repaired the cart and lowered a rod from it.
old_reason: 'Lowered a rod from the cart' is odd, forced word-list; رمّ means to repair but the scenario is contrived; جراج also odd spelling.
reason: رمّ is used for repairing buildings/walls and أنزل منها قضيبًا is an odd collocation; the scene seems assembled from a word list.

arabic: الْمُتَخَصِّصُ السُّورِيُّ يَشْتَغِلُ فِي مَجَالِ الصَّوْتِيَّاتِ، وَهُوَ مَجَالٌ مُعَقَّدٌ جِدًّا.
english: The Syrian specialist works in phonetics, which is a very complex field.
old_reason: Natural and grammatical; phonetics/acoustics field. Translation acceptable.
reason: الصوتيات means acoustics/audio, not phonetics (الصوتيات/علم الأصوات); also المتخصص السوري is fine, but the mistranslation and sense mismatch are problems.

arabic: حَفَلَتِ القَاعَةُ بِالأَعْضَاءِ الأَجَانِبِ أَثْنَاءَ اسْتِضَافَةِ المُؤْتَمَرِ، وَلَا سِيَّمَا مِنَ اليَمَنِ.
english: The hall was crowded with foreign members while it hosted the conference, especially members from Yemen.
old_reason: Grammatical and plausible; حفلت بـ is correct usage.
reason: حفلت بـ is correct; coherent conference scene.

arabic: مَنَحَ الرَّئِيسُ مِلْيُونَ دُولَارٍ لِإِنْشَاءِ صَيْدَلِيَّةٍ لِتَوْفِيرِ الدَّوَاءِ لِلْمُوَاطِنِينَ.
english: The president granted a million dollars to establish a pharmacy to supply medicine to citizens.
old_reason: Plausible news-style sentence; grammar correct.
reason: Correct, coherent sentence.

arabic: غَمَرَتِ الْغِبْطَةُ الطَّبَّاخَ، فَقَدْ تَنَاوَلَ أَصْحَابُهُ الْمَنْسَفَ وَالْمُقَبِّلَاتِ بِحَمَاسٍ.
english: Joy filled the cook, for his friends had eaten the mansaf and appetizers enthusiastically.
old_reason: Tense mismatch: 'تناول' is simple past, and the cook's joy at friends eating is plausible, but the translation uses past perfect 'had eaten'; also 'غمرت الغبطة' is stilted. Translation not exact.
reason: Correct Arabic; غبطة in the sense of joy is attested; the past perfect in English matches the reason clause.

arabic: اِسْتَعَانَ الجَارُ بِمِقَصٍّ وَمُشْطٍ، ثُمَّ اسْتَحَمَّ وَارْتَدَى رِدَاءً نَظِيفًا.
english: The neighbor used scissors and a comb, then bathed and put on a clean robe.
old_reason: Coherent sequence of grooming actions; grammar correct.
reason: Grammatical; scissors and comb then bathing is a plausible grooming sequence, slightly odd.

arabic: تَعِبَ الرَّجُلُ مِنَ التَّزَلُّجِ، وَدَامَتْ مُعَانَاتُهُ مِنَ الْأَلَمِ ثَلَاثِينَ دَقِيقَةً.
english: The man became tired from skiing, and his pain lasted thirty minutes.
old_reason: Awkward: 'his suffering from pain lasted thirty minutes' is unnatural and unspecified; stilted forced phrasing.
reason: Correct and understandable; ordinary scene.

arabic: لَمْ يَتَوَقَّعِ الْأَصْدِقَاءُ مَشَقَّةً فِي الْعَوْدَةِ مِنْ لُبْنَانَ فِي الْجُمْعَةِ الْمُقْبِلَةِ.
english: The friends did not expect any difficulty returning from Lebanon next Friday.
old_reason: Grammatical and plausible, though future time with past negation is fine.
reason: Correct Arabic and translation; ordinary scene.

arabic: الجَدَّةُ صَبُورٌ دَائِماً، وَلِسَانُهَا مُؤَنِّبٌ لَكِنَّهُ مُهَدِّئٌ لِلأَطْفَالِ.
english: Grandmother is always patient, and her tongue is reproachful but calming to the children.
old_reason: الجدة صبور: adjective صبور can be used for feminine without ta marbuta, so that's okay, but 'her tongue is reproachful but calming to children' is a forced, odd combination; مؤنِّب as describing a tongue is awkward.
reason: الجدة صبور: فعول يستوي فيه المذكر والمؤنث فهذا مقبول، لكن «لسانها مؤنِّب ... مهدّئ للأطفال» متناقض ومركّب تركيبًا غير مألوف؛ المؤنِّب لا يهدّئ الأطفال، والجملة غير منسجمة.

arabic: أَمَامَ عِنَادِ الوَلَدِ وَلَامُبَالَاتِهِ كَانَ المُؤَنِّبُ الصَّبُورُ مُفْحَمًا جِدًّا.
english: Before the boy's stubbornness and indifference, the patient reproacher was completely silenced.
old_reason: 'The patient reproacher' is a forced word-list construction; a reproacher being patient and silenced is contrived and awkward.
reason: «المؤنِّب الصبور» اسم فاعل مستخدم كلقب اصطناعي، والسياق مصطنع؛ كما أن «مفحَم» (مسكَت) مع عناد الولد غير دقيق.

arabic: عَانَقَ الْوَالِدُ الصَّيَّادَ الَّذِي نَجَّى ابْنَهُ مِنْ ضِرَاوَةِ التَّيَّارِ.
english: The father hugged the fisherman who had saved his son from the ferocious current.
old_reason: Grammatical, coherent, natural scene; translation accurate.
reason: جملة سليمة وعادية.

arabic: تَنَاوَلَ الطَّحَّانُ مُبَكِّراً سَنْدَوِيتْشًا وَكَرُوَاسُونًا، ثُمَّ كَنَسَ المَطْحَنَةَ.
english: The miller ate a sandwich and a croissant early, then swept the mill.
old_reason: Simple, plausible sentence; grammatical and translation accurate.
reason: العربية سليمة؛ الطحان يأكل سندويتشًا وكرواسان مشهد غير مألوف قليلًا، والتقاء الكلمات يبدو من قائمة مفردات.

arabic: نَظَّمَتِ الفِرْقَةُ مُؤْتَمَرًا، وَشَمِلَ تَوْفِيرُ الاِسْتِضَافَةِ كُلَّ الأَعْضَاءِ.
english: The group organized a conference, and providing hosting included all the members.
old_reason: 'Providing hosting included all the members' is a stilted, forced word-list sentence; الفرقة organizing a conference is odd and the two clauses are disconnected.
reason: «شمل توفير الاستضافة كل الأعضاء» ركيك وغير مألوف، والفرقة تنظم مؤتمرًا بشكل غريب؛ أسلوب إداري مصطنع.

arabic: بِسُرُورٍ، شَاهَدَ الْجَارُ عَوْدَةَ السِّنْجَابِ الَّذِي أَنْقَذَهُ مِنَ الشَّبَكَةِ.
english: The neighbor watched with delight as the squirrel he had rescued from the net returned.
old_reason: Grammatical and coherent story-like sentence; translation accurate.
reason: جملة صحيحة؛ مشهد عودة سنجاب أنقذه الجار غير معتاد.

arabic: هَذَا اللُّغْزُ فِي سُطُورِ الْقِصَّةِ مَصْدَرُ تَشْوِيقٍ لَا مَثِيلَ لَهُ.
english: This mystery within the story’s lines creates unparalleled suspense.
old_reason: 'This mystery within the story's lines is a source of suspense' is clunky and forced; اللغز في سطور القصة is unnatural phrasing.
reason: «اللغز في سطور القصة» تركيب متكلف، و«مصدر تشويق» مقبول لكن الجملة تبدو مصطنعة وغير سلسة.

arabic: كَانَ الْعَبْدُ فِي سِجْنِ مَلِكٍ قَاسٍ، وَقَدْ شَاخَ وَنَحُلَ.
english: The slave was in a cruel king's prison, having grown old and thin.
old_reason: Grammatical and coherent; شاخ ونحل plausible narrative description; translation accurate.
reason: جملة سليمة: شاخ ونحل صحيحان.

arabic: عِنْدَ إِيَابِ الوَالِدِ عَانَقَتْهُ الفَتَاةُ، فَدَامَتْ هَذِهِ الذِّكْرَى مَعَهَا حَتَّى شَبَّتْ.
english: When the father returned, the girl hugged him, and this memory stayed with her until she grew up.
old_reason: Grammatical, coherent narrative; شبّت is used appropriately for a girl growing up; translation accurate.
reason: جملة سليمة ومفهومة؛ إياب وشبّت مستعملان بشكل صحيح.

arabic: أَضَاءَ الهِلَالُ المَدِينَةَ، وَكَانَتِ الصَّائِمَاتُ فِي مِزَاجٍ رَائِعٍ.
english: The crescent lit up the city, and the fasting women were in a wonderful mood.
old_reason: The crescent 'lit up the city' is odd, and the link to fasting women's mood is forced; the feminine plural الصائمات specifically is contrived.
reason: العربية سليمة؛ «أضاء الهلال المدينة» مبالغة شعرية، والصائمات فقط غريب نوعًا ما.

arabic: لَعَلَّ الدَّلِيلَ الَّذِي قَدِمَ مَعَنَا يَهْدِي الوَفْدَ إِلَى المَطْعَمِ.
english: Perhaps the guide who came with us will lead the delegation to the restaurant.
old_reason: Grammatical and plausible; لعل with the indicative verb is acceptable in this context; translation accurate.
reason: جملة سليمة؛ لعل مع المضارع صحيح.

arabic: بَاحَ الشَّيْخُ بِمُعَانَاتِهِ فِي سِجْنٍ قَاسٍ شَاخَ فِيهِ.
english: The old man revealed his suffering in a harsh prison in which he grew old.
old_reason: Grammatical and coherent; plausible statement; translation accurate.
reason: باح بمعاناته صحيح (باح بالسر/الألم)، والجملة سليمة.

arabic: عَاقَبَ المُشْرِفُ الطَّالِبَ البَائِسَ، لَكِنَّهُ لَمْ يَطْرُدْهُ بَعْدَ فَشَلِهِ فِي الامْتِحَانِ.
english: The supervisor punished the miserable student, but he did not expel him after his failure in the exam.
old_reason: Grammatical and plausible school scenario; 'miserable' for البائس is acceptable.
reason: Correct Arabic; ordinary scene. 'البائس' is slightly odd but fine.

arabic: بَعْدَ أَنْ ابْتَلَعَ الصَّبِيُّ الْقَمْحَ، سَعَلَ وَتَعِبَ جِدًّا.
english: After swallowing the wheat, the boy coughed and became very tired.
old_reason: Swallowing wheat grains and coughing is an odd, forced scenario; 'became very tired' doesn't follow coherently.
reason: Grammatical; swallowing wheat and coughing is an odd scene.

arabic: لَمْ يُنَاسِبْ هَذَا الطَّقْمُ مَقَاسَ الوَلَدِ، فَغَيَّظَهُ شِرَاؤُهُ.
english: This set did not suit the boy's size, so buying it made him angry.
old_reason: Plausible: a set of clothes didn't fit, and buying it annoyed him. Grammar fine.
reason: Correct; طقم is a colloquial/loan-ish word for a suit/set, acceptable. غيّظه fine.

arabic: عَجِبَ الطَّالِبُ مِنْ ذَنَبِ الطَّاوُوسِ الَّذِي دَارَ هُنَا فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
english: The student marveled at the tail of the peacock that turned around here in the morning.
old_reason: A peacock's tail 'turning around here' is awkward and illogical (the tail doesn't turn); forced word combination.
reason: Grammatical; 'peacock's tail that turned around here' is odd, but understandable.

arabic: طَحَنَ الجَارُ الخَرْدَلَ وَخَلَطَهُ بِالثُّومِ ثُمَّ عَبَأَهُ فِي كُوبٍ.
english: The neighbor ground the mustard, mixed it with garlic, and then filled a cup with it.
old_reason: Filling a cup with ground mustard and garlic is odd (a jar would be used), and 'عبأه في كوب' means filled it into a cup, not 'filled a cup with it' as translated. Forced.
reason: Grammatical; filling a cup with ground mustard and garlic is odd.

arabic: عَجِبَ الوَلَدُ مِنْ ضِيَاءِ الهِلَالِ، ثُمَّ أَفَلَ الهِلَالُ فَشَعَرَ بِالحُزْنِ.
english: The boy marveled at the crescent's glow, then the crescent set and he felt sad.
old_reason: Coherent, poetic and grammatical; crescent setting makes the boy sad.
reason: Correct and natural; أفل is used for the moon setting.

arabic: هَاتِ نِصْفَ قِطْعَةِ الزُّبْدَةِ الَّتِي غَلَّفَتْهَا الْجَدَّةُ فِي وَرَقَةٍ.
english: Bring half the piece of butter that Grandma wrapped in paper.
old_reason: Natural imperative; wrapping butter in paper by grandma is plausible. Translation accurate.
reason: Correct imperative هات, relative clause agrees; ordinary scene.

arabic: قَلَعَ الجَدُّ الشَّوْكَةَ مِنْ سَبَّابَةِ الوَلَدِ، فَصَمَتَ الوَلَدُ مِنَ الخَوْفِ.
english: Grandfather pulled the thorn out of the boy's index finger, and the boy went quiet out of fear.
old_reason: Plausible scene; going quiet from fear while a thorn is pulled is coherent.
reason: Correct; سبابة is the index finger. Silence from fear is plausible.

arabic: لَاحَ بَهَاءُ القِنْدِيلِ المُنْعَكِسِ عَلَى الطَّاقِ المُسْتَدِيرِ فِي الرُّكْنِ.
english: The brilliance of the lantern, reflected on the round arch, gleamed in the corner.
old_reason: Literary but a forced stack of descriptive nouns; lantern light reflecting on a round arch is contrived and awkward.
reason: Grammatical, poetic; the lantern reflected on an arch is an unusual scene.

arabic: أَيْنَ شَهَادَةُ الطَّالِبِ الَّذِي أَنْهَى الِاخْتِبَارَ بِجِدٍّ وَرَضِيَ عَنْهُ الْمُشْرِفُ؟
english: Where is the certificate of the student who completed the test diligently and pleased the supervisor?
old_reason: Grammatical and plausible question; رضي عنه المشرف means the supervisor was satisfied with him, 'pleased' is fine.
reason: Arabic is fine, but 'رضي عنه المشرف' means the supervisor was satisfied with him, not 'pleased the supervisor' as the English has it.

arabic: رَغِبَ الْأَمِيرُ فِي الطَّاعَةِ، لَكِنَّهُ سَالَمَ الثَّائِرَ وَمَنَعَ الصِّرَاعَ.
english: The prince wanted obedience, but he made peace with the rebel and prevented conflict.
old_reason: The 'but' contrast is incoherent: wanting obedience doesn't contrast with making peace with a rebel; forced word list.
reason: Correct Arabic; 'لكنه' contrast is slightly loose but understandable.

arabic: اِسْتَحْيَا الوَلَدُ مِنْ قُبْلَةِ الجَدَّةِ فَهَمَسَ لَهَا وَلَمْ يَكُنْ زَعْلَانَ.
english: The boy felt shy at his grandmother's kiss, so he whispered to her and was not upset.
old_reason: Mixes colloquial 'زعلان' with formal MSA, and the logic of whispering and not being upset is incoherent.
reason: Colloquial زعلان is accepted; the scene is a bit odd but understandable.
